drivingQuestion: From where is it derived that a paid bailee does not pay for them?
outcomeNote: the answer continues in the next unit

segments.he: נוֹשֵׂא שָׂכָר אֵינוֹ מְשַׁלֵּם וְכוּ׳. מְנָהָנֵי מִילֵּי? דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״כִּי יִתֵּן אִישׁ אֶל רֵעֵהוּ״ – כְּלָל, ״חֲמוֹר אוֹ שׁוֹר אוֹ שֶׂה״ – פָּרַט, ״וְכׇל בְּהֵמָה לִשְׁמוֹר״ – חָזַר וְכָלַל.
segments.en: The mishna continues: «A paid bailee does not pay» if these items were stolen or lost. The Gemara asks: «From where are these matters» derived? The Gemara answers: It is «as the Sages taught» in a baraita with regard to the verse that discusses a paid bailee: “When a man delivers to his neighbor a donkey, or an ox, or a sheep, or any beast to safeguard, and it dies, or is hurt, or is driven away, no man seeing it, the oath of the Lord shall be between them both…but if it be stolen from him, he shall make restitution to its owner” (Exodus 22:9–11). «“When a man delivers to his neighbor”» is «a generalization; “a donkey, or an ox, or a sheep”» is «a detail.» And when the verse states: «“Or any beast to safeguard,” it then generalizes» again.
